title: 9.5 Making Inferences from Sample Surveys

icans: I can estimate a population mean or proportion from a sample.
I can find and interpret the margin of error.
I can use the margin of error to judge a claim.

vocab: use a sample to make ______________ about a population
about ±1/√n for a __________ sample of size n
sample percent ± margin of error: likely to contain the _____________ percent

blocks.sec: Part 1 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

blocks.stem: A random sample of 8 students’ study times (minutes): 30, 45, 20, 60, 35, 40, 25, 45. Estimate the mean study time of all the students.
In a random sample of 250 voters, 140 support a measure. Estimate the percent of all voters who support it.

notes: The interval: Interval = sample percent __________ margin of error
Sample size: A larger sample makes the margin of error _______________.

blocks.stem: In a random sample of 400 voters, 56% support a measure. Find the margin of error and the interval likely to contain the percent of all voters who support it.
Find the margin of error for a sample of 1,600 people.

tickets.stem: Find the margin of error for a sample of 625.
A random sample of 2,500 people finds that 40% prefer brand X. Find the interval likely to contain the population percent.
